Severe Floods Disrupt Transport and Trade Across Sri Lanka

COLOMBO, June 12 – Torrential rains have triggered widespread flooding across Sri Lanka, disrupting transport networks, shuttering markets and halting much of the country’s economic activity, according to officials and local trade associations.

The Disaster Management Centre (DMC) said on Wednesday that at least 15 districts, including Colombo, Gampaha, Kalutara, and Kandy, remain under a flood warning as swollen rivers inundate low-lying areas. More than 200,000 people have been affected, with over 40,000 displaced from their homes and seeking shelter in emergency camps.

Roads and rail lines have been submerged or washed out in parts of the Western and Central provinces, forcing authorities to suspend train services on key commuter routes and close several highways. “The movement of goods and people has been severely hampered, particularly in and around Colombo, where water levels continue to rise,” said Suresh Perera, director of operations at the Sri Lanka Road Transport Authority.

The port of Colombo, one of South Asia’s busiest transshipment hubs, remains open but with limited operations. “Container movement is facing delays of up to 48 hours as access roads are flooded and truck drivers are unable to reach the terminal,” said Anura Jayasinghe, spokesman for Lanka Port Services.

In rural areas, flooding has destroyed paddy fields and vegetable farms at the outset of the Yala harvest season. The All Island Farmers’ Federation reported extensive crop losses in the Kurunegala and Anuradhapura districts. “We are still assessing the damage, but initial estimates suggest that up to 30 percent of the season’s rice crop may be lost if the waters do not recede soon,” said federation president L. M. Wijesiri.

Retail businesses and wholesale markets in Colombo and other major towns remained closed for a third consecutive day. The Sri Lanka National Chamber of Commerce warned that prolonged disruptions could affect supply chains for essential goods. “If transport is not restored quickly, we may see shortages and price spikes in basic commodities,” said chamber chairperson Manori De Silva.

Authorities have deployed military units to assist with evacuations and distribute relief supplies. The Meteorological Department forecasts continued heavy rainfall across central and western regions over the next 48 hours, raising concerns that flood conditions could worsen.

“We urge all residents in affected areas to remain vigilant and follow official instructions,” said DMC chief Mahesh Gunasekara. “The situation remains fluid and our priority is to ensure the safety of all Sri Lankans.”
